findings: Root cause: `legacyImportSender.ts`'s `sendOrderCreatedFromImport` omits the `currency` field entirely from its POST to `/webhooks/order-created`, while `webhookSender.ts`'s `sendOrderCreated` (normal checkout path) always includes it — this directly and fully explains why partner crashes occur only for orders from the bulk CSV import tool and never for checkout orders.

Partner's `consumer.ts` calls `payload.currency.toUpperCase()` with no null/undefined guard, so a missing `currency` field throws a TypeError immediately; this is the proximate crash mechanism, and it means the partner's code is fragile to any future field omission, not just this one.

The v2 docs assert currency is 'always present per the docs,' but this guarantee is violated by the platform's own legacy sender — the documented contract is not actually enforced across all internal code paths that produce webhook payloads for the same documented event.

Two independent, divergent implementations (`sendOrderCreated` and `sendOrderCreatedFromImport`) both POST to the same `/webhooks/order-created` endpoint with no shared payload-construction or schema-validation layer between them; this structural duplication is why the v2 field addition landed in only one sender, and it creates risk that a future v3 change will again be applied inconsistently.

`sendOrderCreatedFromImport` predates v2 ('written before v2 existed') and was evidently never migrated when the currency field was introduced — this looks like a missed rollout/migration step rather than an isolated coding slip, and simply appending `order.currency` may be insufficient if bulk-imported orders don't reliably capture a currency value at the source (CSV import may need an explicit currency default or backfill in addition to a payload fix).

The reported 'intermittent' behavior is not timing- or race-based: it is fully deterministic, occurring on 100% of webhook deliveries from the CSV-import path and 0% from checkout, because the two paths run entirely separate code. This rules out race-condition/ordering theories and means the fix can be validated deterministically by code path alone.

That this schema mismatch reached the partner in production indicates no contract/integration test validates outgoing webhook payloads from both sender code paths against the documented v2 schema before release — a recurring risk for any future documented-field additions.
